text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Serbia's exports will exceed two million dollars this year, says Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.
- Yugoslavia accorded the most favoured nation status in trade with Russia during the visit of Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic to Moscow.
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic to visit Romania on September 20-22.
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic opens Montenegrin trade office in Washington.
- Novi Sad international agriculture fair to be held from September 17 to 21.
- Yugoslav exports up 6.5 percent in first eight months this year on last year, says Federal Statistics Office.
- PTT Serbia is a firm which enjoys confidence in the world, says Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic at the inauguration of a new telephone exchange in Krusevac.
- Yugoslavia expects U.N.-imposed sanctions to be lifted on September 24 because it has done everything to implement the Dayton agreement, says federal trade minister Djordje Siradovic.
- Serbian parliament to endorse government proposal on reduction of social security benefits by 4.1 percent at its September 18 session.
- Everything is ready to transport refugees living in Yugoslavia to vote in Bosnia, schedule of train and bus departures drawn up.
- International mediator for succession of the former Yugoslavia Sir Arthur Watts to visit Belgrade in early October to talk with Yugoslav delegation.
- Albanian-Serbian mixed commission on implementing the agreement on the return of ethnic Albanian students to regular schools expected to meet by the end of the week, probably in Italy.
- Bijeljina in northeastern Bosnia will be a big transit centre in the next three days with trains arriving every hour bringing refugees living in Serbia to vote.
